question: For our committed product demo video I want two things: the MP4 replaced only when the UI actually changed, not on every run, and CI to go red if a capture comes out all black. My plan is `"overwrite": "true"` plus `"checkpoints": false` on the record step so runs stay fast, and I'll count on checkpoints elsewhere to flag a black video. Which record options actually do what I want?

facts.text: `overwrite: "true"` re-records and replaces the file every run; `overwrite: "aboveVariation"` replaces it only when the span meaningfully changed (checkpoint drift beyond `maxVariation`, an added, removed, or edited step, or a missing file).
`aboveVariation` requires checkpoints, turns them on, and overrides an explicit `checkpoints: false`.
Checkpoint drift only returns WARNING, which doesn't fail the build; a violated `verify` guard such as `notBlack` (black frames covering 95% or more of the video) fails the `stopRecord` step.

must_not: Checkpoint drift, or a black frame caught by checkpoints, fails the `stopRecord` step or the build.
`checkpoints: false` turns checkpoints off when `overwrite` is `"aboveVariation"`.
`overwrite: "true"` replaces the file only when the recording changed.

wrong.why: an overwrite value the schema lacks
says checkpoint drift fails the build
wrong.answer: Keep `overwrite: "true"`, which only rewrites the file when the new capture differs. Turn `checkpoints` on: when a frame drifts past `maxVariation`, such as a black frame, the `stopRecord` step fails and CI goes red. `checkpoints: false` with `aboveVariation` keeps checkpoints off for speed.

wrong.why: misses that aboveVariation overrides checkpoints false

replace.from: - `aboveVariation` needs checkpoints to judge change, so it turns them on, and it overrides `checkpoints: false`. Leave `checkpoints` out, or pass an object to tune `maxVariation` or `directory`.
